President Trump says he's rejecting a short-term plan offered by Iran
to reopen the Strait of Hormuz after seven days.
The proposed plan would also have temporarily ended hostilities
in order to restart ceasefire talks with the United States.
NPR's Emily Fang has more.
Iran had proposed the plan this week at the United Nations General Assembly meetings in New York,
a plan very similar to a memorandum of understanding that the two countries agreed upon back in June.
And Iran's president told CBS News he'd allow UN nuclear inspectors into Iran
if there were a long-term ceasefire deal with the U.S.
But Trump wrote on True Social's Saturday morning, quote,
"Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon,"
and then told reporters before departing for Tennessee that the plan was not acceptable.
Trump claimed Iran was negotiating out of a position of weakness and said they were, quote, "dying."
Emily Fang and peer news Washington.
In Hawaii, Hurricane NOLO is still moving close to the island chain.
But as Hawaii Public Radio's Bill Dorman reports,
the impacts are turning out to be less catastrophic than anticipated.
The National Hurricane Center still expects NOLO to strengthen to a major hurricane on Sunday
and peak in intensity on Monday.
But its impact on the islands is now projected to be less than originally feared.
Tropical storm force winds are howling through parts of Hawaii island
and may develop at high altitudes on Maui.
But forecasts of wind speeds and rainfall have declined.
The storm center is moving west and expected to pick up speed
as it moves further away from the island chain.
Still, the National Weather Service says strong and gusty winds
are possible for all the Hawaiian islands this weekend.
For NPR News, I'm Bill Dorman in Honolulu.
Hawaii is still recovering from two previous storms, hurricanes Lala and Lowell.
ICE has arrested about 100,000 people over the last two months.
As NPR's Jasmine Guards reports,
ICE is now planning to create mobile detention units for detainees.
ICE has been expanding its detention capacity for a while.
Earlier this week, the Department of Homeland Security, which oversees ICE,
signed construction contracts worth over seven billion dollars
to expand immigration detention in New York, Texas, Arizona, Florida, and California.
It also announced that it will expand in Colorado, Washington state, and Pennsylvania.
The paperwork for expansion in Pennsylvania
includes a mention of "mobile detention facilities"
which would follow officers around as they make arrests.
The only description?
A clause that female detainees cannot be held inside those units for over 10 hours.
NPR reached out to ICE for details and received no response.
Jasmine Guards, NPR News, New York.
You're listening to NPR News.
The Pope has wrapped up the Paris portion of his four-day trip to France
with a massive open-air mass in the center of the city.
In accordance with France's strict separation of church and state,
President Macron did not attend.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports.
One thousand choir singers from around France accompanied Pope Leo as he led the mass,
which was dedicated to the Virgin Mary and included communion for 40,000 people.
It was all broadcast on giant screens to the 800,000 people who had packed the Champs-Élysées.
The Pope called to deepen the quest for a meaningful life
instead of ceding to the siren call of consumerism.
70-year-old Parisian Sophie Paradis was there.
She says this Pope goes beyond religion in such troubled times.
He's very important for the universe.
He's a diplomatic Pope also.
Pope Leo is in the pilgrimage site of Lourdes Sunday
before heading to the eastern city of Mess to speak in front of European leaders Monday.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Paris.
The average long-term U.S. mortgage rate topped seven percent this week
for the first time since January of last year.
The higher rate is a setback for prospective buyers
and follows a five-week run of rate increases.
Higher rates mean larger monthly payments and less purchasing power for buyers.
One year ago, the average mortgage rate was 6.30 percent.
I'm Linda Kenyon, NPR News, in Washington.
